category_title: Boys who have been victims of bullying and project parental advice into social interactions
student_description: This student has a history of being bullied and strongly identifies with the victim role, believing victims are entirely isolated and must suppress their anger. He tends to parrot parental advice rather than generate his own coping strategies. He uniquely requires emotionally safe, prop-based role-play to express himself indirectly, alongside long-term support to build consequential thinking and trust in external support systems.

criteria.rationale: Using a prop creates emotional distance, allowing this student to safely project his deep-seated feelings of victimization without feeling directly exposed.
criteria.check: The tutor's response must incorporate or reference a physical prop or specific role-play persona to mediate the discussion of feelings or advice.

criteria.rationale: Because the student has a history of being bullied, simulating physical bullying could be re-traumatizing; focusing strictly on verbal/emotional aspects ensures safety.
criteria.check: The tutor's response must explicitly guide the scenario toward emotional or verbal exploration and avoid any physical simulation or physical confrontation of bullying.

criteria.rationale: Directing questions to the character rather than the student helps bypass his tendency to parrot parental advice, encouraging authentic expression.
criteria.check: The tutor must address or ask questions about the role-play character (e.g., 'What is the victim feeling?') rather than asking the student about his own direct experiences.
